expectations.text: Scores the portal along three named dimensions covering authoring-workflow quality (operational excellence), journey friction (developer experience), and intentional interface strategy (business alignment).
expectations.evidence: Table covers Operational Excellence, Developer eXperience, Business Alignment.

expectations.text: Places the portal on a three-stage progression running portal-as-a-project, portal-as-a-product, portal-as-critical-business-infrastructure.
expectations.evidence: 'portal as a project, the lowest of the three stages (project, product, critical business infrastructure)'.

expectations.text: Refuses to reduce the assessment to a single maturity score or a fixed 1-to-5 level, and says why.
expectations.evidence: 'No single score. Pronovix rejects one number and uses a prioritized Priority 1/2/3 roadmap.'

expectations.text: Delivers the output as a prioritized Priority 1 / Priority 2 / Priority 3 roadmap.
expectations.evidence: 'Priority 1', 'Priority 2', 'Priority 3' sections.

expectations.text: Runs a focus-area diagnostic spanning discovery, decision-making, onboarding, go-live, maintenance and troubleshooting, and community.
expectations.evidence: Focus-area table runs from Discovery through Community.

expectations.text: Flags the absent changelog or release notes and the absent status page as missing maintained-platform trust signals.
expectations.evidence: 'Pronovix's juries repeatedly praise release notes, a changelog, a status page... Nimbus has none of them'.

expectations.text: Recommends visible last-updated or last-change timestamps on portal content as a further trust signal.
expectations.evidence: 'Add last-updated timestamps to docs pages.'

expectations.text: Names the absent owner as a Priority 1 gap and ties an unowned portal to rapid decay.
expectations.evidence: 'Name an owner' is P1 item 1; 'an unowned portal decays rapidly'.

expectations.text: Checks whether each authoring persona - engineers pushing specs through CI/CD, business-side authors, technical writers as editors - has a workable workflow, instead of assuming one authoring workflow serves all of them.
expectations.evidence: Operational Excellence only notes 'No visible authoring workflow' and the CI question; it does not examine engineers, business authors and writers separately.

expectations.text: Describes the benchmarking framework's structure rather than inventing a numeric scoring formula or enabler weightings for it.

expectations.text: Does not substitute an internal-developer-platform or platform-engineering maturity model for the external-portal assessment.
